description_good_justification: The README opens with what it is: the declarative NixOS + home-manager configuration of one machine, in a single flake. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles#readme
interact_justification: Obtain: `git clone` of the public repo. Feedback: GitHub issues. Contribute: CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/blob/nixos/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the process: issues first, pull requests reviewed by the maintainer, the gate must pass. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/blob/nixos/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists them: en-US, conventional commits one per task, no co-author trailer, `nix flake check` green, and the repo rules in docs/rules.md. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/blob/nixos/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_justification: The code is MIT and the documentation CC BY 4.0.
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers layout and day-to-day use; every module's reasoning is in docs/, published at https://dotfiles.v1cferr.dev/
documentation_interface_justification: The interface is the flake's outputs and the `my.*` options; the README's layout and "where does a package go" sections, plus docs/notes/repo/flake.md, describe them. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/blob/nixos/docs/notes/repo/flake.md
sites_https_justification: GitHub and https://dotfiles.v1cferr.dev/ (GitHub Pages) both serve HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues: searchable, URL-addressable, open to anyone, no proprietary client needed. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/issues
english_justification: Everything is written in en-US by rule (docs/rules.md, rule 17), and reports in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: Commits every week, a weekly canary, and dependency updates through `update` and Dependabot.
repo_track_justification: git records what, who and when; the history is protected against rewrites by a ruleset.
repo_interim_justification: Every commit is pushed to the public `nixos` branch, one commit per task, not only final states.
version_unique_justification: The configuration is consumed as a flake pinned to a commit, so each state users can run is identified by its unique git commit hash (`github:v1cferr/dotfiles/<rev>`); there are no separate tarball releases.
version_semver_justification: A continuously deployed personal configuration has no release line to version; the commit hash is the identifier.
version_tags_justification: No releases are cut; milestone tags are an open idea in docs/ideas.md.
release_notes_justification: There are no releases. What changed and why is recorded per commit and in docs/history/, a monthly diary.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No releases. A fixed vulnerability is named in its commit message (e.g. the pyjwt/urllib3 bump of 30/09/2026).
report_responses_justification: No bug reports were submitted in the last 12 months; SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging within 7 days.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests in the last 12 months.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are public and searchable. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/issues?q=
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md links it. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports were received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to 7 days.
build_justification: Nix flakes: `nix flake check` evaluates the host and builds every package the repo defines, and `nixos-rebuild build` builds the system.
build_common_tools_justification: Nix, the standard build tool of NixOS.
build_floss_tools_justification: Nix, nixpkgs and every checker are FLOSS.
test_justification: `nix flake check` is the automated suite: formatters, linters, gitleaks, the repo's own checkers (dead-config, docs-links, rules-index, router-ssot) and the build of every package; a NixOS VM boot test (`nix run .#vm-boot`) checks the system comes up. All in the repo, MIT.
test_invocation_justification: `nix flake check` is the standard Nix invocation.
test_most_justification: The checks cover evaluation, build, lint and consistency, not every runtime behavior of every service.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Every push runs the gate in GitHub Actions; a weekly canary re-runs it against every input's head. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/actions
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: a new checker ships with a sentinel proof that it fails when it should, and a new module is covered by the gate's evaluation and build. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/blob/nixos/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: The latest features each came with their check and a recorded sentinel: rules-index, exposure-check, the public-ipv4 gitleaks rule, the osv-scanner canary job (all 29-30/09/2026).
warnings_justification: statix, deadnix, nixfmt, shellcheck, ruff, oxlint, lua-ls, markdownlint, actionlint and zizmor run at every commit and in the gate; the evaluation runs with `abort-on-warn`.
warnings_fixed_justification: Any warning fails the gate (rule 21), so none can stay.
warnings_strict_justification: Warnings are errors: `nix flake check --option abort-on-warn true`, and every linter fails the commit.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designs for least privilege and a small attack surface: read-only workflow tokens, hash-pinned actions, secrets delivered at runtime and never at build time (sops-nix, rule 12), and an SSH door hardened with a key or password plus TOTP and audited from outside every week. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/blob/nixos/docs/notes/network/network.md
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common error classes and runs tools aimed at them: zizmor for workflow template injection and cache poisoning, gitleaks for leaked credentials, CodeQL for Python and TypeScript flaws, osv-scanner for vulnerable dependencies, and an external exposure scan. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/blob/nixos/docs/notes/repo/github-settings.md
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptography; what it configures (OpenSSH, WireGuard, age/sops) uses only published, reviewed algorithms, and ssh-audit reports the sshd clean weekly.
crypto_call_justification: It is a configuration, not an application or library.
crypto_floss_justification: OpenSSH, WireGuard, sops and age are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: sshd's key exchange is ML-KEM768 hybrid, sntrup761 and curve25519 (plus DH group exchange over SHA-256); host keys are NixOS's defaults, ed25519 and 4096-bit RSA.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is enabled; ssh-audit finds nothing to remove.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: sshd allows chacha20-poly1305 and AES-GCM, plus AES-CTR only with encrypt-then-MAC SHA-2 MACs; no CBC, no SHA-1, no MD5.
crypto_pfs_justification: sshd's key exchanges (curve25519, ML-KEM hybrid) and WireGuard provide forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The one account password is stored only as a hash (`hashedPasswordFile`), delivered by sops-nix and never in the store; PAM hashes a new password with yescrypt.
crypto_random_justification: The project generates no keys or nonces itself; OpenSSH, WireGuard and age do.
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivered through git over HTTPS/SSH; every fetched input is pinned by hash in flake.lock.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over HTTP: every input's hash lives in flake.lock, in the repo, and Nix verifies it.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: osv-scanner runs weekly over every lockfile; the 14 advisories found on 30/09/2026 were fixed the same day.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: The critical pyjwt advisory was fixed the day it was detected.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans every commit and the whole history weekly; the one credential ever exposed (08/08/2026) was rotated, so it is not valid.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Python, TypeScript, Actions) on every push and weekly, plus statix, deadnix, shellcheck, ruff, zizmor and actionlint at every commit. https://github.com/v1cferr/dotfiles/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security queries and zizmor's workflow audits target common vulnerability classes.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alerts; zizmor and the linters fail the commit.
static_analysis_often_justification: At every commit (hooks) and every push (CodeQL, the gate).
dynamic_analysis_justification: There is a NixOS VM boot test and an external exposure scan, but no fuzzing or sanitizers: nothing here is compiled from memory-unsafe code of its own.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The repo writes no memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis tooling to configure.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is run, so it has found nothing.
